prompt.context: The client is the North American CEO of a global personal and home care products company. He has hired Capgemini Consulting to turn around the North American business from loss to profitability within two years. The final board presentation is scheduled for this afternoon, but the project team is stranded at an airport and cannot make it. You are asked to step in and make the presentation instead.
prompt.question: Step in for the stranded project team and present the turnaround analysis to the board. Structure your approach, interpret the exhibits provided, and deliver a recommendation to return the North American business to profitability within two years.

clarifying_info.q: What are the main revenue streams?
What are the key cost drivers?
What other internal areas are relevant?
clarifying_info.a: Supply chain, channel strategy, financial situation, org structure, and core competencies.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the main competitors and what segments do they serve?
clarifying_info.a: The case focuses on the North American cosmetics/personal care space; competitors vary by segment and channel.

clarifying_info.q: How intense is rivalry in the cosmetics industry?
clarifying_info.a: Rivalry is significant; there are trends toward consolidation and product/channel diversification.

clarifying_info.q: Through what retail channels are products sold?
clarifying_info.a: Multiple channels exist including direct selling, retail stores, salons, and web; the relative power of retailers is a key consideration.

clarifying_info.q: What are the different consumer segments?
clarifying_info.a: Segments are defined by gender and age group (Baby Boomers, Gen X, Echo Boomers) across Mexico, USA, and Canada.
Consumer trends and perception of necessity vs. luxury affect share of wallet and are shifting over time.

exhibits.title: 2009-2014 Growth in Personal Care Consumption by Age Group
exhibits.shows: A chart showing projected growth in personal care consumption broken down by gender and age group (Baby Boomers, Generation X, Echo Boomers) across three North American regions: Mexico, USA, and Canada.
exhibits.data: Growth rates by female age cohort: Female Baby Boomers — Mexico 8.63%, USA 5.31%, Canada 5.98%; male 55+ shows stronger growth than other male groups; Echo Boomers flagged as a future consumption group.

exhibits.title: Ranking Major Household Spending Categories by Share of Wallet and Perception of Need
exhibits.shows: A scatter/matrix chart plotting major household spending categories on two axes: Share of Wallet (Low to High) on the vertical axis and Perception of Need (Luxury to Necessity) on the horizontal axis. Categories plotted include Taxes, Housing, Food, Insurance/Pension, Clothing, Household Operations, Personal Care, Health Care, Recreation, Education, Donations/Contributions, Tobacco/Alcohol, and Household Furnishings & Equipment.
exhibits.data: Household Products represent 4.5% share of wallet; Personal Care represents 1.7% share of wallet (Canadian census data). Taxes, Housing, and Food occupy the high necessity / high share-of-wallet quadrant.

exhibits.title: Product-Channel Strategy Map
exhibits.shows: A strategy map comparing competitors' channel approaches, distinguishing between companies with a dedicated (single-primary) channel strategy and those with a diverse multi-channel strategy. Examples of competitors and their channel configurations are shown.
exhibits.data: Examples: Estee Lauder uses prestigious retail stores, company-run salons, and brand websites (diverse). The Body Shop has a network of 2,000+ stores as primary channel plus a web channel in North America and a direct selling force (dedicated with secondary channels).

framework: Internal Analysis: Revenue streams (existing vs. new products), cost drivers (R&D, manufacturing, operations), financial situation, org structure, core competencies
Supply Chain & Operations: In-house vs. outsource manufacturing, distribution network design, scalability of distribution centers
Channel Strategy: Current vs. optimal channel mix, alignment of channel strategy to product category breadth
Industry Analysis: Competitive intensity and rivalry, consolidation trends, competitor channel and segment strategies
Customer Analysis: Consumer segmentation by gender and age group, geographic differences within North America, share of wallet and perception of need, changing consumer trends

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 1, what are your key observations about personal care consumption growth by age group and region?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should note: (1) Women dominate personal care consumption across all three regions. (2) Female Baby Boomers are the primary growth engine — generating 8.63%, 5.31%, and 5.98% growth in Mexico, USA, and Canada respectively — driven by large numbers and high spending power from wealth accumulation and inheritance. (3) Male consumption is small but the 55+ male age group shows stronger growth than other male cohorts and should not be ignored. (4) Generation Xers are underrepresented due to relatively small cohort size, except in Mexico which had higher population growth between 1965-1985. (5) Echo Boomers (born 1985-1995) will play a greater role beyond 2010 and should be watched as a future consumption group.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 2, what are your key observations about share of wallet and perception of need for personal care products?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should note: (1) There is a direct co-relationship between share of wallet and consumer perception of need — the more a category is perceived as a necessity, the larger its share of wallet. (2) Personal Care (1.7% share of wallet) and Household Products (4.5%) are positioned as moderate necessity items, well below Taxes, Housing, and Food. (3) From a marketing perspective, the ability to reposition personal care products higher on the necessity axis is essential to capture a larger share of wallet. (4) This insight has direct implications for the client's marketing and brand strategy.

questions.prompt: After reviewing Exhibit 3, what are your key observations about channel strategy in the cosmetics industry?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should note: (1) Companies with dedicated channel strategies often focus on Direct Selling to maximize consumer interaction. (2) There is a trend toward diversification of both product categories and channel strategies — different products require distinct channels and placements. (3) Competitors with diverse strategies (e.g., Estee Lauder: retail stores, salons, brand websites) capture consumers across multiple touchpoints. (4) Competitors with dedicated strategies (e.g., The Body Shop: 2,000+ stores globally plus web and direct selling) use a primary channel with secondary support. (5) Given the client's large number of product categories, a diverse channel strategy appears more appropriate than a dedicated one.

questions.prompt: Beyond the three exhibits, what other considerations should you inform the CEO require further analysis?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should cover: (1) Make vs. Buy (in-house manufacturing or outsource): pros/cons, key constraints and criteria, competitor benchmarks. (2) Customer: impact of country of origin on customer perception relevant to marketing and brand strategy. (3) Location and Distribution Network: does the current network support future growth considering all costs; what distance span optimizes service and costs. (4) Decision Making Process: current state of Make/Buy decisions, what the process should be, who is responsible/accountable. (5) Scalability: how distribution centers will scale with growth projections, number of centers required, optimal range per center.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional considerations should inform the CEO's turnaround strategy beyond the data in the three exhibits?

categories.name: Manufacturing & Operations
ideas: Evaluate in-house vs. outsource manufacturing trade-offs
Assess key constraints such as capital, quality control, and speed-to-market

categories.name: Distribution & Supply Chain
ideas: Redesign distribution network to support future growth
Determine optimal number and location of distribution centers
Analyze distance span to balance service levels and logistics costs
Plan for scalability as volume grows

categories.name: Customer & Brand Strategy
ideas: Assess impact of country of origin on brand perception
Research customer needs to inform product and marketing strategy
Develop segment-specific strategies for Baby Boomers and emerging Echo Boomer cohort

categories.name: Channel Strategy
ideas: Evaluate current channel mix against the diverse product portfolio
Consider adding or investing in under-utilized channels (e.g., e-commerce, salons)
Benchmark Estee Lauder and The Body Shop channel models

categories.name: Decision Making & Governance
ideas: Map current decision-making process for make/buy and channel choices
Define clear ownership and accountability for strategic decisions
Establish governance to align North American operations with global strategy

recommendation: The client should focus on female Baby Boomers, who represent the largest growth segment in personal care consumption across Mexico, USA, and Canada, while also monitoring the growing 55+ male cohort. Geographic differences within North America must be factored into the go-to-market approach.

The client should develop deep knowledge of customer needs, perception, and spending patterns to capture a greater share of wallet. Since personal care currently sits at only 1.7% of wallet, repositioning the category higher on the necessity axis through targeted marketing is critical for sustainable long-term growth.

The client should shift to a more diverse distribution channel strategy. Given the breadth of product categories, a dedicated single-channel approach is misaligned; the client should follow the diversification trend seen among leading competitors.
risks: The market may not continue growing at the predicted rate or may enter a period of decline.
Threat of substitute products and changing customer trends could reduce the perceived necessity of the client's products, shrinking the addressable share of wallet.
next_steps: Invest in customer research to deepen understanding of Baby Boomer and emerging Echo Boomer segments across Mexico, USA, and Canada.
Commission a marketing strategy review to assess how to reposition personal care products higher on the necessity axis.
Conduct a thorough cost-benefit analysis of diversifying distribution channels, including investment requirements and expected returns.
Review and redesign the supply chain and distribution network to ensure it supports growth projections efficiently.
